newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European shares helped up by Dow's 7th peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European shares helped up by Dow's 7th peak.

text.p: Leading European shares traded significantly firmer on Friday, boosted by a seventh consecutive record close on Wall Street overnight.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was softer but off its lows against the mark and steady on the yen in early European trading after Thursday's benign U.S. inflation data.

In New York The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 6,300 points for the first time overnight, energised by the news on U.S. inflation. It closed up 38.76 points at 6,313.00, matching an unbroken string of highs set in February.

London shares opened higher on the back of New York, but dealers said gains were likely to be limited as the domestic market dwelt on Thursday's shock rise in domestic retail prices, which raised the prospect of another British interest rate rise.
Some analysts said the Dow's bull run was giving cause for concern.
"We're all expecting and waiting for Wall Street to consolidate and it's giving us a reason to hold off buying." said one head of equity sales.
"We would like to see just how well our market can tolerate a U.S. consolidation."
In Paris French shares started with a big one percent increase, establishing a fresh year-high for the CAC-40 index, and stocks continued to strengthen.
Dealers said the market was supported by Wall Street as well as by a new contract high in French bond futures.
The French rise takes shares back to early 1994 levels. The life high, at 2,360.98, was reached on February 2, 1994.

It was a similar story in Frankfurt, where German shares opened bourse trade at around record levels, just shy of what dealers described as the psychologically important 2,800 point level. The market was supported by strong dollar, which is good for German exports, and volumes were high, dealers said.
Speculation of mergers or takeovers in the banking sector fuelled much of the trade, with Commerzbank among volume leaders, they said.

On the foreign exchange front, analysts said Thursday's neutral U.S. inflation data, which indicated the Federal Reserve had been correct this week in not moving rates one way or the other, had done the dollar no harm.

The next indicator awaited by the markets was U.S. October industrial production and capacity utilisation numbers, due out at 1415 GMT on Friday, They should confirm the view that the economy is heading for a soft landing, analysts said.

"They (the numbers) should show some more falls which again reinforce the view that U.S. rates are on hold," said Julia Jessop, econmist at Nikko Europe. Despite some slippage of the dollar against the mark, traders said there was good dollar support below 1.50 marks.
"People don't really want to be short of dollars down there because they are wary that the Bundesbank could do something," said a trader at a Japanese bank.

Much of Friday's currency market activity was focused on the pound sterling, which touched a fresh four-year high of 1.6697 dollars and 30-month highs of 1.5096 against the mark as the markets pondered the possibility of higher British interest rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1050 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5057 marks and 111.23 yen compared with 1.5096 marks and 111.31 yen late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1050 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 19.3 points at 3,945.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 20.85 at 2,239.03.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 16.94 at 2,793.59.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted lower at $381.50 compared with $382.50 at the London close on Thursday. Silver was also lower at $4.86.
